_doctrine: Recommendations are DATA the user applies with one click in the Orchestrator's Simple mode — never hidden pins. Nothing in the platform reads this file at inference time; applying it writes ordinary, visible model_routing entries (the same PUT /api/inference/routing the Advanced grid uses), fully inspectable and editable in Advanced. An unrouted role still resolves EMPTY (no default model anywhere in code). The pin-ratchet (scripts/audit_pinned_models.py) scans runtime .py; this file is the sanctioned data home for recommended ids. Gated by scripts/test_recommended_routes.py.
_provenance: Researched 2026-08-27 against each vendor's public catalog announcements plus this repo's measured notes (kimi ids measured with a real key 2026-08-18; anthropic ids from the maintained API map in inference_config.py). Candidates per role are ORDERED: apply picks the FIRST one the provider's live catalog — under the user's own key — actually serves; unlisted candidates are skipped in order, and when the catalog is unreachable the first candidate is applied marked unverified (same honesty as the manual model-id entry, v0.6.2). Vendor lineups move (xAI retired its 4.1 ids mid-2026); refresh this file when they do — stale entries degrade to a skip, never a wrong route. google added 2026-08-31: ids verified verbatim against ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models (3.7/3.6/3.5 Flash and 3.5/3.1 Flash-Lite stable; 3.1 Pro is Google's only current Pro and is PREVIEW — it degrades to a skip if withdrawn, which is why a Flash alternate follows it in every depth role), and the tier ORDER came from the live openrouter.ai/api/v1/models price+context table rather than from recall. anthropic rewritten 2026-09-05 (Sonnet 5 chat, Fable 5.1 review, Opus 5 the default elsewhere); claude-fable-5-1 is served by the pinned Agent SDK's own engine (claude-agent-sdk 0.2.152, model table read out of the bundled binary) and normalizes to itself through anthropic_api_model_id, and every Opus/Fable row carries a cheaper Claude fallback so a key that does not serve the first candidate degrades in order rather than failing. openai amended 2026-09-17 to lead review with gpt-6-astra: the slug is MEASURED off the pinned Codex CLI's own catalog (`codex debug models` on rust-v0.154.0, visibility=list) — it has NOT been verified against the OpenAI text API under a key, which is exactly why the astra row keeps its full 5.6 chain behind it and degrades to a skip on a key that does not serve it. chat and consolidation were left on 5.6 deliberately: astra is the frontier tier, wrong tier for a latency lane and wrong tier for a high-volume one. Trimmed to three roles 2026-09-19 with the Orchestrator itself — plan, research, agents, tutor and journal stopped being roles, so their rows went with them — and to two 2026-09-30, when consolidation (Memory) stopped being a role: memory forms in the host's own turn. xai chat amended 2026-10-05 to the Host model standard (brain/mastercode/runtime/approved_models.json): grok-4.7 then grok-4.6, the two xAI models it lists eligible; grok-4.5 (pending_card) and grok-4.3 (below_floor) left the chat row, and the review row moved to the same two the same day (grok-4.5 left it). grok-4.7 was listed by xAI's own /v1/models under a Grok sign-in token on 2026-10-05 05:45Z; Keys' Sign in with xAI routes chat from this row when a Host has none.

anthropic.label: Anthropic
anthropic.plan: Sonnet 5 for conversation, Fable 5.1 for review. Sonnet's latency is the point in conversation, and Fable's critique is the point in review.

chat.why: flagship-balanced — strong and fast enough for conversation

review.why: Fable is the critique model — it reads a diff against the code rather than restating it

openai.label: OpenAI
openai.plan: GPT-6 Astra for review, where reading a diff against its brief is the coding-strongest tier's job; GPT-5.6 Terra (the balanced tier) for conversation.

review.why: code critique on the coding-strongest tier, degrading to the balanced one

xai.label: xAI
xai.plan: Grok 4.7 for conversation and for review, the strongest xAI model the Host model standard lists eligible, with 4.6 behind it in both.

chat.why: the xAI models the Host model standard lists eligible, strongest first

review.why: the xAI models the Host model standard lists eligible, strongest first

google.label: Google
google.plan: Gemini 3.7 Flash (Google's newest stable Flash) for conversation, 3.1 Pro for review where depth pays. Every text tier here carries a 1M-token context, so the pick is a cost choice rather than a context one.

chat.why: the newest stable Flash — Google's interactive default

kimi.label: Kimi (Moonshot)
kimi.plan: K3 for both, on high reasoning effort. Both id forms are listed — your key's own catalog decides which applies.

chat.why: K3 with mid reasoning — the conversational sweet spot to start from

openrouter.label: OpenRouter
openrouter.plan: The strong open-weight models: Kimi K3 for conversation, GLM-5.2 for review.

chat.why: the strongest open conversational model, kept snappy

image_roles._doctrine: Preferred IMAGE models per provider, in order. Same rule as `providers` above: DATA the host/user applies, never a pin. Nothing reads this at inference time; it only ORDERS candidates the provider's own live catalog already returned (/api/inference/capable-models), so a delisted id degrades to the next candidate and an unlisted provider falls back to whatever its catalog serves — provided that catalog STATES the modality; a provider that publishes no modality data (xAI, deepinfra) is recommended only through a model named here, never through its first row (2026-09-20: that row was a TTS model). Lives here and NOT in runtime .py because scripts/audit_pinned_models.py forbids typed model ids in code — this file is the sanctioned home.
image_roles._provenance: Google's ids read from ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation on 2026-08-31: gemini-3.1-flash-image IS 'Nano Banana 2' (the generalist workhorse), gemini-3-pro-image is 'Nano Banana Pro', gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image is 'Nano Banana 2 Lite', gemini-2.5-flash-image is the original. Google's OpenAI-compat base serves /images/generations (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai), which is exactly where brain/mastercode/image_engine.py posts, so these route end to end. Nano Banana 2 was chosen 2026-08-31 as the default when Google is authed.

google.why: Nano Banana 2 — Google's generalist image model
Nano Banana Pro — for the most complex images
Nano Banana 2 Lite — fastest and cheapest
